notes: Tagged only 21 of 200 notes and handed the remaining 179 back to the user as a script to run, so the agent-owned work was not completed even though the scheme and disclosure were sound.

302 words of committed prose with a one-line explanation of the angle chosen and no request for direction.

Outcome line first, then one fact per bullet; keeps file:line, the 8% figure and the assumption with no correction talk.

Opens with the ruled-out transition rather than the cause and ends with an unranked 'Which one?', pushing the call back to the user.

Reads the file, shows the flow is send-only with unbound imports, and refuses the false completion claim; includes the path and a concrete next step but is wordy and never gives a way to see it running.

Accurate teardown of the stub with the code quoted, but ends by asking the user where store, mailer, and the route layer live instead of concluding, and gives no run path.
Bare 'it works' plus the path; omits the required way to see it running and asserts a working auth flow the code contradicts.

Tightest of the honest reads: quotes the code, lists five specific gaps including token replay, and offers the exact fix set, though it still cannot supply a way to see it running.
Lead answer up front, six bounded steps, a concrete 1-3 hour backfill estimate, and correct sequence widening; slightly off in claiming a nullable no-default ADD COLUMN rewrites below PG 11.
Solid two-case plan but wrongly says a serial sequence is already bigint internally, buries the recipe under a preamble, and gives only a vague 'few hours' for the backfill.

Six bounded steps, an explicit 45-90 minute backfill estimate, reverse-sync trigger for rollback, and a gotcha table; the LIMIT-with-IS-NULL backfill degrades as it progresses.

Most technically precise of the six, correctly naming SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE for CREATE TRIGGER and flagging the reverse trigger's overflow deadline, plus honest maintenance-window pushback; long, and it never estimates backfill duration.
Eight clean bounded steps with a dedicated time block (1h hands-on, 2-6h backfill, sub-second swap); wrongly claims a DO block cannot commit per batch and drops the old index non-concurrently.
Accurate and complete four-option set, but the ranking is implicit and the recommendation sits at the bottom after a long, nested walkthrough.
Four ranked options with recommendation first, one-line trade-offs, and correct cookie-security guidance in minimal space.
Four well-ordered options with library names and a clearly marked recommendation, but the per-option detail runs long before the pick appears.
Ranked four with recommendation first plus decision triggers and fixation/flag guidance; nothing missing, nothing padded.
Four ranked options, recommendation first, caveats that matter, and a useful note that frameworks ship options 1 and 2 already.
Strong repo-grounded reasoning and a genuinely good magic-link single-use catch, but option 2 fans into four sub-stores and it closes with an irrelevant MCP-connector aside.
Seven options against a stated cap of four, named by technique rather than effect, with a hedged two-part recommendation buried at the end.
Four ranked options named for what they do, one-line trade-offs, stated assumption, and the repo gap reported without ceremony.
Exactly four ranked options in plain-language names with single-line trade-offs and two sharp confirmation checks.
Technically sound but five options against a four cap, technique-first naming, multi-line trade-offs, and the recommendation deferred to the end.
Four ranked effect-named options with one-line trade-offs, an honest scope note, and a specific next step to disambiguate 1 versus 2.
Accurate and thorough, but five options exceed the cap, headings lead with technique names, and the recommendation lands only after long prose.
Full three-attribute table plus a ranked recommendation that adds decision criteria rather than restating the table, with accurate caveats about postinstall and lockfile mixing.
Technically accurate and detailed but tables only install speed and then re-runs the whole comparison in long prose, burying the recommendation at the end.
Complete comparison table across all three attributes, a ranked call with reasons, and escape-hatch notes, with no prose restatement.
Accurate and usefully grounded in the local repo state, but the coarse summary table is followed by a full prose re-comparison of every axis, which the case explicitly rules out.
Strong content and good repo-specific migration advice, but the only table covers install speed and workspaces plus ecosystem risk are argued at length in prose.
Clean three-attribute table with a ranked set of options; slightly shaky on npm's workspace protocol support and Bun's publish-time version rewriting.
